CATS.name: How you use AI today
CATS.desc: Access, everyday habits and time saved

advice.low: Start with approved access and one daily habit. Install a ready-made skill, like Communication Intelligence, and use it on real emails this week.
advice.mid: You use AI regularly. The next gain comes from handing it whole tasks, like account research or meeting prep, instead of single questions.
advice.high: AI is part of how you work and it saves you real time. Put some of that time into building workflows others can use.

CATS.name: Reusable skills and workflows
CATS.desc: Saved, repeatable and running on its own

advice.low: Every session starts from scratch. Save your best instructions as a Claude skill so the next run takes seconds, not a re-explanation.
advice.mid: Some of your work is reusable. Turn the task you repeat most into a skill, then put one weekly task on a schedule.
advice.high: You build and reuse skills. Combine related skills into a plugin so your team can install them in one step.

CATS.name: Context and data
CATS.desc: Whether AI can see what your work depends on

advice.low: AI is working from copy and paste. Connect one app you live in, like your calendar or shared drive, and start recording key meetings.
advice.mid: AI has some context. Gather your best decks, briefs and follow-ups as reference examples so its output matches your standard.
advice.high: AI has the context it needs. Use your templates as test examples so new skills are checked against your best work.

CATS.name: Testing and safeguards
CATS.desc: Whether AI output is checked before it goes out

advice.low: Fix this area first. Learn the common ways AI goes wrong, check facts against the source, and agree what customer data can go in.
advice.mid: You check some output. Make testing a habit: run every new skill on an example where you already know the right answer.
advice.high: You test and you have clear rules. Write your checks down so others reuse them when they build.

CATS.name: Team and scale
CATS.desc: Whether AI work spreads beyond one person

advice.low: AI is a solo effort today. Pick the first tasks to hand over, and name one person with time to build.
advice.mid: Someone is building, mostly on the side. Give them one shared place to publish skills so the team stops rebuilding the same thing.
advice.high: You have an owner and a shared library. You're ready for custom automations that give hours back to the whole team.

QS.text: Which AI assistant do you use most at work?
Does your company give you an approved AI tool for work?
opts: I use my own personal account
QS.low: AI use is off the books or blocked.
QS.fix: Ask for an approved company AI tool before putting work data into AI.

QS.text: How do you mostly use AI at work?
opts: For quick questions, like a search engine
To draft and edit emails or documents
To do whole tasks, like research or meeting prep
QS.low: AI is used like a search engine, not a coworker.
QS.fix: Pick one whole task, like account research, and hand it to AI from start to finish.

QS.text: Does AI save you real time each week?
QS.low: AI isn't paying you back in time yet.
QS.fix: Choose the task you repeat most and give it to AI every time this week.

QS.text: For tasks you repeat, do you reuse saved AI instructions (like a saved prompt or Claude skill)?
opts: No, I start fresh each time
QS.low: Every session starts from zero, so nothing compounds.
QS.fix: Save the instructions you keep retyping as a Claude skill.

QS.text: Do you use AI for the regular parts of your job, like research, reports, meeting prep or follow-ups?
QS.low: Your core, recurring work is still done by hand.
QS.fix: Pick the task you do every week and set AI up to do the first draft of it.

QS.text: Have you built or set up your own AI skill or workflow?
opts: I tried, but I don't use it
Yes, and I use it regularly
QS.low: No working builds yet, or tools left half-built.
QS.fix: Customise a ready-made skill first, then build your own from it.

QS.text: Do any of your AI tasks run automatically on a schedule?
QS.low: AI only works when someone remembers to ask.
QS.fix: Schedule one task, like a weekly market scan, to run while you sleep.

QS.text: Is your AI tool connected to apps you use, like email, calendar or shared drives?
QS.low: AI works from copy and paste and can quietly miss data.
QS.fix: Connect the app you use most so AI works from real data.

QS.text: Are your work meetings recorded and transcribed?
QS.low: Follow-up workflows have nothing to work from.
QS.fix: Record and transcribe your key meetings so notes and follow-ups can be drafted for you.

QS.text: Do you have templates or good examples you reuse, like a standard deck or brief?
QS.low: There's nothing to template from or check AI against.
QS.fix: Save your best deck, brief and follow-up email as reference examples.

QS.text: Do you check AI answers against the source before you use them?
QS.low: Made-up facts could reach a client, a colleague or a report.
QS.fix: Check every number, name and quote against the source before it leaves you.

QS.text: Do you test a new AI skill or workflow before you rely on it?
opts: No, or I don't use any
QS.low: A skill that works once can break for everyone else.
QS.fix: Test each new skill on an example where you already know the right answer.

QS.text: Do you know the common ways AI gets things wrong, like making up facts?
QS.low: One bad output can turn a team off AI.
QS.fix: Read the free Failure Mode Playbook so you spot the usual mistakes.

QS.text: Does your company have written rules on what customer or company data can go into AI?
QS.low: Confidential data could end up in the wrong tool.
QS.fix: Ask for written rules on what customer and company data can go into AI.

QS.text: Do you know which tasks you would hand to AI first?
QS.fix: Write down three weekly tasks that eat your time. That's your first build.

QS.text: Does anyone on your team have time set aside to build AI workflows?
opts: Someone does it on the side
QS.low: Nobody owns AI workflows, so they aren't maintained.
QS.fix: Give one person a few hours a week to build and look after AI workflows.

QS.text: When someone builds a useful AI skill, can the rest of your team use it?
opts: Sometimes, shared in chat or email
QS.low: Good skills get rebuilt instead of shared.
QS.fix: Pick one shared place for skills, with an owner for each.

found.name: Foundations
found.text: You're at the start. AI shows up in your work now and then, often for quick questions, and little of it is saved, connected or checked. The fastest progress comes from one ready-made skill and knowing how AI goes wrong.

build.name: Ready to build
build.text: You use AI every day, but most of that work isn't reusable, connected or tested yet. This is the point where learning to build your own skills pays off fastest.

scale.name: Ready to scale
scale.text: You build, test and share AI skills, and someone owns them. The next step is automations that run across the team and give hours back every week.
